chapter: Opinions on pop music, jazz education and the business
title: Rock emphasis at Berklee and Hinton's hope for new outlets
summary: Ted Jr. objects to rock emphasis, Wilson cites falling rock sales, and Hinton hopes theatre and dance could use jazz.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: How the music business changed: hype, youth and lost apprenticeship

blocks.x: They emphasize too much on rock, as far as I'm concerned.
Well, they're gonna have to read the
newest issue of Variety and see if the rock movement can sell some more records, because they're firing a lot of people in the studios. In the rock recording studios, yes.

But the jazz sales and the classical sales are holding steady. But the pop thing is taking a big dive, But they are worried -- the top three companies are worried; they need that new gimmick to sell another gold record.

Perhaps.. since we got these young people -- we got to find some places for them to work. To get the -- change the concept of television programs and Broadway shows, if we've got these kind of young people coming out of these universities and doing these things, perhaps we can get some young writers to think along this line. This is my hope, this is my dream, as an old man -- for the preservation and continuation of jazz. If you do it, Steven, and you do it, Teddy, Junior, and so many other people are doing this, there must be some in dance. I think perhaps it ... go ahead.
The Alvin Ailey Ballet is considering doing some things. They did one of Mingus's things.
